newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Witness says missing Ethiopian journalist tortured.
newsitem.headline: Witness says missing Ethiopian journalist tortured.

text.p: A driver has told an Addis Ababa court he saw missing Ethiopian author and journalist Baalu Girma in severe pain after being tortured by the ruling military junta in the 1980s.

The 54-year-old driver's testimony on Thursday at the trial of former members of the Dergue military junta was the first news of Baalu since the U.S.-educated former deputy information minister went missing more than 20 years ago.
Seventy-one former Dergue military junta officials accused of genocide and crimes against humanity are on trial in the capital. They face the death penalty if they are found guilty.
Only 46 of the 71 accused are in court. The others including dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam, who ruled Ethiopia from 1977 to 1991 and now lives in Zaimbabwe, are being tried in absentia.
"I saw Baalu Girma severly tortured and in great pain as I was driving him from Dergue Headquarters to Bermuda house," said the driver, who works for the Central Investigation Office.
Bermuda house was a torture and detention centre, so-named because many the people taken there were never seen again.
"I drove Baalu Girma three times from Bermuda to the dergue investigation headquarters...The investigators covered Baalu's face with hoods while he was being transported," the driver said.
Baalu, a leading Ethiopian journalist and author, was a deputy minister under the Dergue until he wrote a book exposing the horrors of the military junta's rule.
He was dismissed from his post before he disappeared.
The witness, who under court rules cannot be identified by name, said he was driving through Addis Ababa in 1986 with a Dergue "hit squad" when they spotted a girl and boy walking.
He said a major who led the squad asked him to stop.
"He went to the couple and shot to death the girl with three bullets in open daylight," he said. He added the boy was dumped by members of the hit squad in the car and had later disappeared.
The trial was adjourned on Thursday until next Tuesday.
Ethiopian prosecutors have charged 5,198 people with war crimes, aggravated homicide and genocide under the Dergue.
